title: Refuse in the Tool, Not in the Prompt
tagline: Move a broken rule into the tool — but only where the tool can actually check it.

story.problem: A research specialist recorded a caterer with the inquiry address inquiries@hideseekmedia.com, read off a WeddingWire page for a different business. Outreach runs live, so that address was one plan away from a real stranger's inbox — and the scout's instructions already forbade directory sources and already required a published address on the vendor's own site.
story.solution: record_vendor refuses at the write boundary: a source URL on any of 20 known directories, matched on host labels rather than as a substring of the URL; an email whose corporate domain shares nothing with the vendor's name or website, with free mail passing untouched; and a source page that returns a definitive 404 or 410. Every refusal returns a note naming the next action. The counter-lesson is enforced too — a required drive time, which no tool in the system can produce, was demoted to an optional field the scout is explicitly told never to search for. When the prose rule decayed under measurement, the radius came back as arithmetic: record_vendor geocodes the vendor's town against the couple's and refuses beyond the straight-line miles the stated drive covers, failing open wherever it cannot judge.
story.outcome: The guards are unit-tested without a model against real rows from a production run: the findings the scout eval caught reject, and every legitimate finding from the same run still passes, including gmail addresses and contact-form-only vendors. Removing the unreachable drive-time requirement read 52/53 with the radius judge at 100% on the day it was measured; a later settled run measured the prose rule failing, and the distance guard's first runs read five refusals with every recorded vendor within 38 straight-line miles, then 49/54 (91%) with 13 of 14 within 40.

prerequisites: This repository cloned and npm install run once
Network access: the liveness guard issues one real GET per recorded vendor
No model key for the guard suite — the checks are pure functions plus one fetch
No local key for npm run eval:scout either — it drives the deployed Venus, whose keys live on the deployment

quickstart.configure: npm install — the guard suite needs no API key; add .env.local only if you go on to npm run eval:scout
